variable: New feature (~9000 LOC, agent-written) enabled on both client and server; smallest production rollout (~5000 hosts in one datacenter). Client-side P99 latency regressed within ~10 minutes of the flag flip.
control: Same code with the feature flag disabled on client and server.

facts.observation: Client DNS lookup for the storage service returned ~400 addresses in the variable, ~5 in the control.

provenance.source: live production host, DNS lookups observed during client monitoring

facts.observation: Cross-datacenter TCP session establishment time did not differ between control and variable (tens of milliseconds in both).

provenance.source: tcpdump on a flag-on client host plus a flag-off client against a flag-off server

facts.observation: Server-side P99 latency regressed in aggregate graphs.
The TLS certificate is loaded once during initial session establishment, not per RPC call (verified by monitoring the running process in both variable and control).

provenance.source: process monitoring on a live flag-on client host

hypotheses.text: Server reloads the TLS certificate on every RPC call over the established session, adding per-call cost.
The new mTLS codepaths bypass the sharded database client, so requests route to a random pod which then fetches from or forwards to the correct shard, inflating tail latency on both reads and writes.
Server-side capacity degradation or event-loop stalls.
